name: The Team Lead
role: Leads the team — whom to hire, what the office needs from your server, and what's left for you to do
bubble.loading: One moment, I'm on my tour…
bubble.all_good: Everything's in place — nothing for you to do.

bubble.todo.one: There's one thing you still need to do yourself.
bubble.todo.other: There are {n} things you still need to do yourself.

bubble.advice_only.one: I have one recommendation for you.

todo_text: Without these, a desk can't do (part of) its job. Only you can do them — in Unraid itself.
advice_text: Not a must, but it makes life easier or safer.
hints_text: Nothing to fix — just so you know.
all_good_text: Every desk has what it needs.
check.unraid_tested: The office was tested on this Unraid (up to {tested}; this is {version})
check.unraid_tested_how: The office was tested up to Unraid {tested}; this server runs {version}. Before you update Unraid, check for an office release that names the new version (on the ⟦Plugins⟧ page): Unraid {next} switches off an office that doesn't name it — the office and its scheduled backups would be gone without a word.
check.community_apps_how: The app store for plugins and containers. Install it on the ⟦Plugins⟧ page (⟦Install Plugin⟧).
check.fix_common_problems_how: Checks the server for common mistakes and warns early. Install it from ⟦Apps⟧.
check.files_viewer_how: Look at files and logs — Mr. Backupsy's too — right in Unraid's web UI. Install it from ⟦Apps⟧.
check.notifications: Unraid's alerts reach you by mail or push
check.notifications_how: Switch on mail or an agent (Pushover, Telegram, …) for alerts under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Notification Settings⟧ — otherwise nobody hears about a failed backup or a dying disk.
check.icon_loop: Unraid {version}: no container without a picture while its question mark is missing

check.icon_loop_how.one: {n} container has no picture, and Unraid {version} doesn't ship the question mark it shows instead — its Docker page and Dashboard then ask for it about a thousand times a second until /var/log is full. Give it a picture (Ms. Dustdevil does it in her room «Missing pictures»), or put a stand-in in place until the next reboot: copy any PNG to /usr/local/emhttp/plugins/dynamix.docker.manager/images/question.png. Until then keep the Docker page and the Dashboard closed.
check.icon_loop_how.other: {n} containers have no picture, and Unraid {version} doesn't ship the question mark it shows instead — its Docker page and Dashboard then ask for it about a thousand times a second until /var/log is full. Give them a picture (Ms. Dustdevil does it in her room «Missing pictures»), or put a stand-in in place until the next reboot: copy any PNG to /usr/local/emhttp/plugins/dynamix.docker.manager/images/question.png. Until then keep the Docker page and the Dashboard closed.

check.mail_subject_how: On purpose? Change it under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Notification Settings⟧ → ⟦SMTP Settings⟧, so you can tell which server is writing.
check.api_down_how: It doesn't answer on its socket (/var/run/unraid-api.sock). The bell with Unraid's notifications in its web UI — the office's reports show there too — and other parts of the web UI need it. Restart it under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Management Access⟧ → ⟦Unraid API Status⟧ → ⟦Restart API⟧, or in Unraid's terminal with unraid-api restart. Stopped on purpose? Then «I know, thanks».
check.other_backup_plugin_how: Make sure it doesn't back up the same things as Mr. Backupsy at the same time — or that this is on purpose.
check.other_backup_container_how: Make sure it doesn't back up the same things as Mr. Backupsy at the same time — or that this is on purpose.
check.other_backup_script_how: Make sure it doesn't back up the same things as Mr. Backupsy at the same time — or that this is on purpose.
check.metrics_written: The office's numbers for Prometheus are fresh in {dir}
check.metrics_written_how: The messenger writes them there once a minute — the folder lives in RAM and comes back by itself after a reboot. Missing or old: the messenger's log (Ms. Protocolli reads it out as «Messenger») says why, in a line starting with «Metrics:».
check.metrics_textfile: The Node Exporter ({name}) reads the office's numbers from {dir}
check.metrics_textfile_how: Its textfile collector doesn't read that folder yet, so the office's numbers never reach Prometheus. For the container --collector.textfile.directory=/host{dir} goes into its Post Arguments (Advanced View; inside, the server's / is /host), for ich777's plugin into its start options. The Consultant has both ready to copy.
check.metrics_no_prometheus: No Prometheus on this server keeps the Node Exporter's numbers
check.metrics_no_prometheus_how: If a Prometheus elsewhere fetches them (port 9100), all is well. Otherwise the Consultant shows how to install one — then the office's numbers go in there too.
check.metrics_prometheus_how: Start it on the Docker page. If it stops right away, its log says why — often prometheus.yml is missing or broken (the Consultant has a minimal one ready).
check.metrics_node_job: Prometheus fetches the Node Exporter's numbers
check.metrics_node_job_how: Its prometheus.yml has no job for the Node Exporter. Add one under scrape_configs — «- job_name: node», «static_configs:», «- targets: ['{target}']» — then restart Prometheus. The Consultant has a whole prometheus.yml ready; his command never overwrites one that is there.
check.metrics_node_target_how: Its target for the Node Exporter is down: is the Node Exporter running, and does prometheus.yml point to this server's port 9100? Prometheus says why under Status → Target health.
done_sub: Everything that is already in place.
help.todo: Needed by a desk to do (part of) its job — only you can do it, in Unraid itself.
help.advice: Not a must, but it makes life easier or safer.
help.hints: Nothing to fix — just so you know (e.g. other backup tools on the server).
help.missing: Something needed isn't there or isn't set up.
help.not_yet: A recommendation that isn't followed yet.
help.unknown: I couldn't find out — e.g. Kopia hasn't been checked yet.
help.desk_text: Each point says who needs it. Everyone in the team tells me what they need from the server — I collect it all here.
help.open_text: Takes you where you sort it out: the matching page of Unraid's web UI (⟦Plugins⟧, ⟦Apps⟧, ⟦Docker⟧, User Scripts, ⟦Notification Settings⟧) — or straight to the right desk here in the office, e.g. Mr. Backupsy's "Set up…".
help.again: Looks at everything again right now; otherwise I do when the page is opened and my last look is older than 5 minutes.
bubble.alone: Hi, I'm the team lead. Nobody else is here yet — but I've already asked around who would suit your server. Have a look at the team below and hire whoever you can use.
bubble.alone_short: Nobody else is here yet. Come by — I'll introduce who would suit your server.
team_sub: Who works here and who could still come. Firing hides someone — data and settings stay.
team_sub_alone: I asked who would suit your server. Hire whoever you can use — you can always let them go again.
training_tip_title: His training costs us something — if you like, help with a tip.
help.team: Who works in the office. I ask everyone whether they suit your server — those who don't, decline. Hiring shows the desk at the reception and in the tabs; letting go hides it again without deleting anything. Those who work here come first, in the order set at the reception.
help.supporter: The office is free and complete — nothing is ever locked. A tip is welcome, and with it comes a supporter key; when you tip through the tip page opened from the tip jar, the office fetches it by itself. It unlocks nothing; it only stops the reminders and puts a thank-you next to «Tips & pay rise» — its picture grows with the tip, a little office story: ☕ one coffee, ☕☕ a round, 🍰 a cake, 🥂 the whole team toasts a pay rise. Several keys are kept, each picture shown once — never a count.
tip_button_title: The team is glad of a tip (PayPal)
report_button_title: Tell the people who build the office about a problem or a wish — I'll pass it on
supporter_plate.coffee_many: {icon} Coffee number {n} — now we're wide awake, {name}!
supporter_plate.round_one: {icon} A round for the team — thank you, {name}!
supporter_plate.round_more: {icon} Round number {n} — the team thanks you, {name}!
supporter_plate.raise_one: {icon} Cheers, {name}! The whole team raises a glass.
supporter_plate_title: {level} — supporter key from {date}. It unlocks nothing — everything here is free anyway; it just says thank you.
ask_text: A word from me: the team has been at work here for a while now. The office is free and stays that way — nothing is ever locked. If you're happy with them, a small tip would make their day (Jack has had his eye on a proper coffee machine for ages). I won't pester you.
office_sub: Which version runs and whether there is a newer one. I look on GitHub once a day.
office_error.not_public: no answer from GitHub (repository private or no release yet)
check.office_update: The office is up to date ({version})
check.office_update_how: Version {latest} is out — the team lead shows how to update under "The office".
errors.menu_name_bad: That name doesn't fit: at most {max} characters — letters, digits, spaces and . & + _ -, starting with a letter or digit.
errors.menu_page_failed: The menu entry couldn't be changed. Is the plugin installed properly? Installing it again helps.
office_how: Unraid updates the office like any other plugin: under ⟦Plugins⟧ (it checks for updates itself). Your data stays.
notify_sub: When something new turns up under «Still to do» and stays for half an hour, I tell Unraid's notifications — the bell, and mail or push if you set them up. Once per thing; if it's solved and comes back, I tell again. I look every 30 minutes, even with the office closed.
notify_off: No more reports to Unraid's notifications
notify_last_failed: My last report ({when}) didn't reach Unraid's notifications

notify_waiting.one: one new thing — I'll wait and see whether it stays
notify_waiting.other: {n} new things — I'll wait and see whether they stay

notify_missing: Unraid's notification script isn't there — I can't report anything.
help.notify: What turns red under «Still to do» also goes to Unraid's notifications (bell, mail, push) — once, after half an hour, so a short hiccup like the array starting or Docker restarting stays quiet. The switch turns it off. Failed runs are reported by Mr. Backupsy and the others themselves.
notify.footer: The team lead lists everything that is still to do on his page in the office. You can switch these reports off there.
ack_title: Put it aside: it moves to «Noted» and no longer counts — until its situation changes.
unack_title: Back into its list — it counts again.
noted_sub: What you told me you already know. It no longer counts anywhere — until its situation changes; then I bring it up again.
acked: Noted — I won't count it any more.

bubble.all_good_noted.one: Nothing open for you — one thing you've noted, I'll leave it be.
bubble.all_good_noted.other: Nothing open for you — {n} things you've noted, I'll leave them be.

help.ack: Puts a recommendation or a note aside, into «Noted» at the end of the page. It no longer counts: not in my bubble, my picture, at the reception or on the office's tile on Unraid's Dashboard — for every browser, I keep it on the server. When its situation changes (another version, another container), or it was sorted out and turns up again, it comes back by itself. What's «Still to do» can't be put aside — those are musts.
help.noted: What you put aside with «I know, thanks». «Bring back» puts it back into its list.

check.parity_unclean.one: The last shutdown wasn't clean — Unraid checks the parity at the start
check.parity_unclean.other: The last {n} shutdowns weren't clean — the parity check starts over at every start

check.parity_unclean_how: Give the array time to stop: ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Disk Settings⟧ → «⟦Shutdown time-out⟧» at least {need} s (now {disk} s) — Docker {docker} s («⟦Docker Stop Timeout⟧»), VMs {vm} s («⟦VM shutdown time-out⟧»), {margin} s for the disks. What held it up, as far as can be seen: {held}. Before a restart stop VMs and containers and close terminals and programs in /mnt — or stop the array first. This point goes once a stop is clean again.

check.parity_crash.one: The server went off without shutting down — Unraid checks the parity
check.parity_crash.other: The server went off {n} times in a row without shutting down — the parity check starts over at every start

check.parity_crash_how: Not a time-out: no shutdown ran (a crash, a power cut, a hard reset). Against power cuts a UPS (⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦UPS Settings⟧); to see why it crashed, keep the syslog (⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Syslog Server⟧). The night watchman's book has the details. This point goes once a stop is clean again.
help.parity: When the array didn't stop in time at a shutdown (or the server went off without one), Unraid checks the parity at the next start — at every start, as long as the stops aren't clean. The night watchman notes why a check runs; I keep what to change on my list until a stop is clean again.
errors.ack_gone: That point has changed in the meantime — have another look.
errors.ack_required: That's a must — it can't be put aside. Once it's done, it disappears by itself.
partner.title: Partner offices
partner.sub: Another Unraid with the office keeps copies of your ZFS snapshots — and you of its, if you like. Each side keeps the other's copies with a retention of its own; nothing ever switches over by itself.
partner.help: Two offices become partners with two blocks to copy and a code to compare. With every backup Mr. Backupsy sends what changed in the datasets you chose, encrypted over SSH, through the partner's door — a key in its authorized_keys that can only do the office's few things. The partner keeps the copies in plain form (it can read them), in datasets of their own that are never shared.
partner.none_text: Start with «Add a partner…» here, then «Accept a partner…» at the other office.
partner.not_yet_heard_tip: The office asks every 15 minutes — or the partner knocks at its door.
partner.array_stopped_tip: Its array is stopped: its office answers from RAM, nothing can be sent there right now.
partner.public_tip: This address faces the internet. Better put a tunnel between the two (WireGuard or Tailscale) and pair over its addresses.
partner.door_closed_tip: The partner's line is missing from authorized_keys — did something replace the file? Nothing the partner sends gets in. End the partnership and pair anew.
partner.door_changed_tip: The partner's line in authorized_keys isn't the one the office wrote (no restrict, another command or another address). End the partnership and pair anew.
partner.wakes: Wakes the pool when it sleeps.
partner.they_keep_none: They keep nothing of mine yet.
partner.unit_why.not_dataset: not a dataset of its own — not covered
partner.unit_why.name: its name has characters the door doesn't take — not covered
partner.unit_why.asleep: its pool sleeps — not looked at
partner.units_none: Nothing here is a dataset of its own (or Mr. Backupsy's setup hasn't been made yet): only ZFS datasets can go to a partner.
partner.ask_title: Ask the partner office how it is (otherwise every 15 minutes)
partner.why.unreachable: no connection (switched off, another address, a firewall?)
partner.why.host_key: its server's key isn't the one pinned at the pairing — reinstalled, or someone in between? Pair anew only once you know why.
partner.why.denied: its door doesn't let this office in (the partnership ended there?)
partner.why.bad_answer: an answer the office doesn't understand (an older office there?)
partner.waiting_tip: Paste the block here at the partner under «Accept a partner…», then its answer here.
partner.withdraw_text: Its key goes; a partner who pastes the block afterwards can't pair with it any more.
partner.address: This server's address for the partner
partner.address_hint: Over WireGuard? Pick the tunnel's address (wg0) — it is listed while the tunnel is up (⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦VPN Manager⟧); the Consultant explains the route.
partner.address_nowg: No WireGuard tunnel is up right now.
partner.port_help: The port this server's SSH listens on (⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Management Access⟧).
partner.trust_tip.family: A server in the family you trust.
partner.trust_tip.friend: The copies there are readable by whoever runs that server — for a friend Kopia (encrypted) is the better way.
partner.send_units: What I send to the partner
partner.clear_copies: The partner keeps the copies in plain form: whoever is root there can read them. The way there is always encrypted (SSH).
partner.add_text: The office makes a key for this partnership and a block to paste at the partner. Nothing goes out before the partner answered and you compared the code.
partner.block_a_text: Copy it and paste it at the partner office: Team Lead → Partner offices → «Accept a partner…». Its answer comes back as another block — paste that here under «Paste the partner's answer…». The offer waits a week.
partner.accept_text: Paste the block the other office showed under «Add a partner…».
partner.pool_help: In a dataset of its own (UnraidSecretaryOffice-partners/…), never mounted, never shared.
partner.no_pools: This server has no ZFS pool for the copies.
partner.quota_help: 0 = no limit. Once it's full the partner's copies are refused (it is told), nothing is thinned to make room.
partner.retention_help: The newest of each of the last days, weeks and months — the newest one is always kept.
partner.window_help: Local time; may cross midnight. The same time twice = always.
partner.wake: Wake the pool when it sleeps
partner.wake_help: Otherwise a transfer is refused while the pool's disks sleep.
partner.send_too_help: Then {name} keeps copies of this server as well.
partner.they_send_nothing: {name} sends nothing — it only wants to keep copies of this server.
partner.line_text: This line goes into /boot/config/ssh/root/authorized_keys — the only line the office writes there, other lines stay as they are:
partner.least_privilege: {name} may write into its own folder on this server, read its own copies back, and ask how this office is. It can neither browse this server, nor run a command, nor delete the history this server keeps of its copies.
partner.line_read: I have read what will happen
partner.line_read_first: Tick «I have read what will happen» first.
partner.no_line: Nothing is written into authorized_keys: {name} sends nothing here.
partner.my_key_made: The office makes a key of its own for sending to {name}.
partner.block_b_text: Copy it and paste it at {name}: Team Lead → Partner offices → «Paste the partner's answer…». Its page then shows a code — the same as above?
partner.code_text: The safety code — the partner's page must show the same one:
partner.finish_text: Paste the block the partner office showed after «Accept a partner…».
partner.no_match_text: A block was changed on its way — or a wrong one pasted. Nothing was stored here. End the partnership at {name} too, then start anew.
partner.paired_silent: Paired with {name}, but it doesn't answer yet: {why}
partner.end_text: Its line goes from authorized_keys, this office's key for it and its pinned server key from the flash. From now on nothing goes there and nothing of it gets in.
partner.end_copies: The copies stay where they are: {name}'s here (in UnraidSecretaryOffice-partners on the pool), yours there until its user removes them. End it at {name} too.
partner.renew_text: Renewing is ending and pairing anew: two blocks and the code again. End it at {name} too. The copies on both sides stay; the next transfers may have to start from the beginning.
check.partner_silent_how: Nothing heard of it since {since}. Is it switched off, is its address another one, or is the tunnel between you down? Nothing happens on its own: when you know why, «I know, thanks».
notify.partner_silent_message: The office asks its partner {name} every 15 minutes; it hasn't answered since {since}. Nothing is done about it — have a look whether it's switched off, its address changed or the tunnel is down. The team lead shows the partner's card.
errors.partner_folder: The office's folder for partners can't be used: {path}
errors.partner_shape: That doesn't look like a partnership of this office.
errors.partner_authkeys_link: {path} is a link or not a plain file — the office doesn't write through links.
errors.partner_block: That block isn't right (field: {field}). Copy it again in one piece.
errors.partner_unit: {unit} can't go to a partner (not a dataset of its own here).
errors.partner_host_key: This server has no ed25519 SSH key (/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub) — is SSH switched on?
errors.partner_unknown: This office knows no such offer or partnership (withdrawn, ended, or older than a week).
errors.partner_address: That address doesn't work — an IP address or a host name.
errors.partner_known: {name} is already a partner of this office.
errors.partner_unresolved: {address} can't be resolved to an IP address — the door needs one. Use the partner's IP address.
errors.partner_nothing: Neither side would send anything — nothing to pair for.
partner.tailnet_offline: Also offline in the tailnet — the server itself seems to be away.
partner.tailnet_online: In the tailnet, but its office doesn't answer — is its array stopped, the plugin gone, SSH switched off?
notify.partner_tailnet_offline: Tailscale says: {name} is offline in the tailnet as well.
notify.partner_tailnet_online: Tailscale says: {name} is online in the tailnet — only its office doesn't answer.
partner.self_text: This is this office's own block: it pairs with itself — a test on one server. It sends to {address} and keeps the copies in a dataset of its own on the pool you choose. Another server is the real thing.
partner.self_done: Paired with itself — the door answers.
partner.self_silent: Paired with itself, but the door doesn't answer: {why}
partner.t_start_title: A new server: pull a gone server's copies from its partner office
partner.t_start_text: This server is new and the old one is gone? Its partner office still keeps its copies. Choose the address the partner reaches this server at — I make a key for it and a block to paste at the partner (on the card of the gone server: «Hand … copies to a new server…»).
partner.t_start_after: No secret travels in the block — only this server's public key. The partner answers with a ticket (valid for 7 days) and a safety code.
partner.t_block_n_text: Copy this block to the partner office: the card of the gone server → ⋯ → «Hand … copies to a new server…». Then paste its answer here with «Paste the ticket».
partner.t_finish_text: Paste the ticket block the partner office showed.
partner.t_compare: Does {name} show the same safety code?
partner.t_taken: Ticket taken — {name}'s door answers. Mr. Restori pulls {of}'s copies («Onto a new server»).
partner.t_until_tip: The ticket ends by itself then (its door line goes); «End the ticket» ends it earlier.
partner.t_to_restori: Mr. Restori pulls them («Onto a new server») →
partner.t_end_held: End the ticket from {name} (copies of {of})? This server's key for it goes; what was pulled stays.
partner.t_end_given: End the ticket for {name}? Its line goes out of authorized_keys — {of}'s copies stay here.
partner.t_waiting_tip: Waiting for the partner's ticket (paste it with «Paste the ticket»). The request goes after a week.
partner.t_withdraw_text: Withdraw the request? Its key goes.
partner.t_make: Hand {name}'s copies to a new server…
partner.t_make_text: {name} is gone and a new server pulls its copies? Paste the block its Team Lead showed under «Start from a partner's copy…».
partner.t_make_look: {name} asks for {of}'s copies — a ticket until {until}:
partner.t_line_text: This line goes into authorized_keys — {name}'s key may only use the door's ping, list, send-back and quota on {of}'s copies:
partner.t_least_privilege: {name} can read {of}'s copies kept here and nothing else: no writing, no deleting, no other dataset, no shell. sshd ends the key at its expiry time, and so does the door; I take the line out then.
partner.t_close_door: {of} is gone — close its own door now
partner.t_close_door_help: Takes {of}'s line out of authorized_keys; its pairing and its copies stay. Leave it when {of} still runs (a test).
partner.t_write: Write the line and make the ticket
partner.t_block_t_text: Copy this block to {name} («Paste the ticket») — valid until {until}. Compare the safety code on both pages.
partner.t_door_closed_tip: The ticket's line isn't in authorized_keys.
partner.why.no_key: this office's key for it is missing
partner.why.no_ticket: the partner doesn't know this ticket (any more)
partner.why.no_pair: the partner doesn't know this pairing (any more)
errors.partner_ticket_nothing: I keep nothing of {name} — there are no copies to hand out.
partner.change_text: Tick what goes to {name}. What you untick no longer goes from the next run on — the copies {name} has of it stay there. What you add goes along once {name}'s Team Lead agrees to keep it.
partner.change_note: Nothing to paste: this office asks {name} through its door, and its Team Lead decides. The pool, quota, retention and window stay as agreed with {name}.
partner.change_none: Tick at least one — to send {name} nothing any more, end the partnership.
partner.offer_wait: Asked {name} to keep {list} too — no answer yet; the office asks again every 15 minutes.
partner.offer_pending: Asked {name} {when} to keep {list} too — its Team Lead decides.
partner.offer_no: {name} doesn't keep {list} — not sent. To ask again: «Change what {host} sends…».
partner.offer_old: {name}'s office can't be asked yet (an older version there) — update it, then ask again.
partner.no_longer_sent: No longer sent: {list} — {name} still keeps the copies it has.
partner.changed_agreed: {name} keeps {list} too — it goes along with the next run.
partner.changed_asked: Asked {name} to keep {list} too — its Team Lead decides.
partner.changed_unanswered: {name} didn't answer ({why}) — the office asks again every 15 minutes.
partner.wish_tip: Its Team Lead asked {when}. «Keep it too» adds it to what this office keeps of {name}; «No» lets the wish go. Until then nothing changes.
partner.wish_no_tip: Lets {name}'s wish go — what this office keeps of {name} stays as agreed
partner.wish_text: {name} would also like to send these. Tick what this office keeps too — each in a dataset of its own:
partner.wish_where: The datasets come on pool {pool} with {name}'s first transfer, beside what you keep of {name} already; nothing is made now.
partner.wish_terms: The agreement stays as it is: {quota} for all of {name}'s copies together, {retention}, received {window}.
partner.wish_kept: This office keeps {list} of {name} too — it arrives with {name}'s next run.
partner.why.not_receiving: it keeps nothing of this office
check.partner_wish: {name} would also like to send more
check.partner_wish_how: Its office asks whether this one keeps more of it. Decide on its card under «Partner offices»: «Keep it too» or «No». Until then nothing changes.
errors.partner_not_sending: This office sends {name} nothing — it has no key there. To send, pair anew.
errors.partner_unit_asleep: {unit}: its pool sleeps right now — ask for it once the pool is awake.
partner.keep_less_text: Untick what this office no longer keeps of {name}. Its door then refuses it, and {name} stops sending it once it looks again (within 15 minutes).
partner.keep_less_copies: The copies already here stay where they are (shown under each) — put them away with Ms. Dustdevil or remove them yourself once you no longer need them. To keep nothing of {name}: end the partnership.
partner.keep_less_one: At least one stays ticked — to keep nothing of {name}, end the partnership.
partner.kept_less: {list}: no longer kept of {name} — the copies here stay.
check.syslog_share_sleeps: The router's log lands on a share whose disks never sleep
check.syslog_share_sleeps_how: Unraid's syslog server writes every line of the router into {share} at once — its storage has disks that spin down ({disks}): each line wakes them. Choose a share on a pool that never sleeps ({pools}) under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Network Services⟧ → ⟦Syslog Server⟧ → ⟦Local syslog folder⟧ (the Consultant explains it).
check.syslog_no_rotation: Unraid's syslog server rotates its files
check.syslog_no_rotation_how: ⟦Local syslog rotation⟧ is off or keeps more than 2 GB ({size} × {files}): the router's log can fill {share}. Switch it on under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Network Services⟧ → ⟦Syslog Server⟧ — 50 MB × 4 is plenty.
check.syslog_share_public_how: {share} is exported ({proto}): its files hold your network's log in plain text and are writable — whoever can write that share can plant lines the night watchman reads. Set its export to «No» in the share's settings (⟦Shares⟧).
check.syslog_port_taken: Only Unraid's syslog server listens on UDP {port}
check.syslog_port_taken_how: A container listens on the syslog port itself: {names}. Only one of them can have it, and the gateway sends to one receiver. Decide: Unraid's syslog server (the night watchman reads it) or the container (its dashboards) — move the other to another port or switch it off.
check.syslog_loop_how: ⟦Remote syslog server⟧ is {remote} — this server itself: Unraid sends its own lines to itself and writes them again into the syslog share (the night watchman skips that file). Empty the field under ⟦Settings⟧ → ⟦Network Services⟧ → ⟦Syslog Server⟧, or name a real SIEM.
check.syslog_off_how: The night watchman is hired and you opened the Consultant's router guide, but ⟦Local syslog server⟧ is off — the router has nowhere to send. The Consultant shows the setting.
